stories.title: NBA’s Dallas Mavericks Seek Zoning for Sports and Entertainment District
stories.excerpt: The Dallas Mavericks’ chose a likely place to begin the rezoning process for a sports and entertainment district, a onetime thriving mall. The team is looking at 100 acres of land that used to be the Valley View Center. The mall was once home to Bloomingdale’s, Dillard’s and Macy’s in the 1990’s but was shuttered and then demolished in 2023. The Dallas Business Journal reports the team says it’s looking for a vibrant mixed-use destination anchored by a state-of-the-art arena, along with restaurants, entertainment options, public green spaces and family-friendly experiences. The Mavs have until January 2028 to close on the land. Seritage Growth Partners owns a portion of the Valley View site. Mavericks ownership is paying $126,900 per month through January 2027, which increases to $274,950 through January 2028, for the right to buy the land. The agreement calls for Arena Development Intermediate LLC, or ADI, a Mavs subsidiary overseeing the deal, to ultimately pay around $51 million to purchase the site. The post NBA’s Dallas Mavericks Seek Zoning for Sports and Entertainment District appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Dallas Mavericks seeking zoning for 100-acre mixed-use sports/entertainment district on Valley View Center site
ADI (Mavs subsidiary) paying $51M to acquire former mall demolition site; closes January 2028
Project includes arena, restaurants, entertainment, green space; signals major Dallas infill redevelopment
stories.summary: The Dallas Mavericks are pursuing zoning approval for a mixed-use sports and entertainment district on 100 acres of the former Valley View Center mall in Dallas, demolished in 2023. Through subsidiary Arena Development Intermediate LLC, the team has agreed to pay approximately $51 million for the site, with closing targeted for January 2028. The planned development will anchor around a state-of-the-art arena, complemented by restaurants, entertainment venues, public green spaces, and family-friendly amenities.
stories.impact: Major infill redevelopment signals strong institutional confidence in Dallas real estate fundamentals and downtown activation. The zoning rezoning of a large former retail site to mixed-use creates ripple demand for nearby multifamily; the arena and entertainment anchor will drive employment concentration and young professional attraction to that submarket, supporting rent growth and absorption for residential projects within 2–3 miles of the Valley View site.

stories.title: Harrison Street Hires Dan Fanelli as Co-Head of U.S. Investment Solutions in NYC
stories.excerpt: Harrison Street Asset Management is appointing three new executives to lead its strategies in the U.S., Asia and Europe. Dan Fanelli will join the global investment management firm as managing director and co-head of its Investor Solutions Group. Fanelli’s move comes after stints at PGIM, Brookfield Asset Management and Innovo Property Group, according to Harrison Street. Dan Kim also joins Harrison Street as managing director in Chicago focused on infrastructure. Kim previously led consultant relations for eqt partners. “As the firm continues to grow globally, we remain committed to investing in exceptional talent and strengthening our Investor Solutions platform to best serve our clients,” Geoff Regnery, co-president of Harrison Street’s Investor Solutions Group, said in a statement. “These appointments reflect the continued evolution of our global team and our focus on deepening relationships with institutional investors around the world as we continue to scale our platform.” James Choi has also been promoted from Harrison Street’s head of Asia based in Tokyo. He will be moving to the West Coast to work alongside Fanelli as his co-head and focus on “deepening relationships with North American institutional clients,” according to the company. “These appointments bring together seasoned leaders with deep institutional relationships and complementary expertise across real estate, infrastructure and credit,” Jenna Sheehan, co-head of the Investor Solutions Group, said in a statement. Harrison Street, founded in part by Christopher Merrill, has over $110 billion in assets, mostly consisting of student housing, senior housing and medical offices, and has offloaded about $6 billion in properties over the last 12 months, Commercial Observer previously reported. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Harrison Street hires Dan Fanelli as co-head U.S. Investment Solutions; background includes PGIM, Brookfield
No specific capital deployment or market focus announced; leadership hire signals firm scaling
Limited direct relevance to multifamily development fundamentals or market conditions
stories.summary: Harrison Street Asset Management has appointed Dan Fanelli as managing director and co-head of its Investor Solutions Group, along with complementary senior hires in Chicago and Asia. Fanelli brings experience from PGIM, Brookfield Asset Management, and Innovo Property Group. The firm is expanding its platform to deepen relationships with institutional investors globally.
stories.impact: Organizational talent moves at large capital platforms are not directly actionable for development teams unless tied to specific product focus, capital deployment strategy, or market emphasis. This announcement signals Harrison Street's growth but does not provide market-level demand, supply, or capital availability signals relevant to multifamily underwriting.

stories.title: LORE and Element Land $58M to Build Miami Condo
stories.excerpt: Lore Development Group and Element Development have nabbed a $58 million construction loan for a boutique condo project in Miami’s coveted Coconut Grove neighborhood. SME Capital provided the 30-month senior financing, which includes two six-month extension options, backing the eight-story development called the Lincoln. The project is set to include 48 units at 2650 Lincoln Avenue, adjacent to Southwest 27th Avenue, near the neighborhood’s commercial center. Amenities will include a rooftop pool and valet parking. Construction started in June and is expected to be completed in the third quarter of 2028. Berkadia’s Scott Wadler, Bobby Dockerty, Mitch Sinberg, Matt Robbins and Brad Williamson brokered the debt. So far, 40 percent of the units have pre-sold, with One Sotheby’s International Realty serving as the head broker. LORE Development Group, a joint venture between Miami-based Leste Group and Brazil’s Opportunity Fundo de Investimento Imobiliário, purchased the 0.5-acre site for $8.6 million in 2023, according to property records. Coconut Grove has become one of Miami’s most sought-after neighborhoods. Last year, Google’s billionaire co-founder Larry Page spent roughly $188 million assembling a compound in the ritzy enclave. Other developers are also banking on the demand. In January, Terra and AB Asset Management secured $410 million to build a nearby, 194-unit boutique luxury condo. That same month, CMC Group and Fort Partners scored a $323.8 million construction loan for a Four Seasons-branded condo along the waterfront. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: LORE Development and Element Development secure $58M construction loan for 48-unit condo in Coconut Grove, Miami
SME Capital provides 30-month senior debt; 40% pre-sold; completion Q3 2028

stories.summary: LORE Development Group and Element Development have closed a $58 million construction loan from SME Capital for The Lincoln, an eight-story, 48-unit boutique condo project in Coconut Grove, Miami. The project began construction in June with expected completion in Q3 2028. Pre-sales have reached 40 percent, with One Sotheby's International Realty handling brokerage.
stories.impact: Strong construction financing availability and presale velocity (40% sold pre-completion) in Miami's Coconut Grove submarket signals sustained residential demand and lender confidence in condo absorption. For multifamily developers, this validates rental upside and occupancy fundamentals in Miami, but also indicates capital competition from condo conversion and high-end projects; developers eyeing Coconut Grove or adjacent neighborhoods should expect higher land costs and increased competitive pressure.

stories.title: Madison Realty Capital Lends $77M for Whole Foods-Anchored Texas Development
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between Trademark Property Company and Harrison Street Asset Management has sealed $77 million of construction financing to build a mixed-use development in the Dallas-Fort Worth region anchored by Whole Foods, Commercial Observer has learned. Madison Realty Capital originated the loan for the sponsorship’s Shivers Farm project in Southlake, Texas, featuring 37 single-family residential lots along with 161,000 square feet of retail and office space. The development will include a 35,500-square-foot Whole Foods that marks the grocer’s first location in Southlake. Located at 1900 North White Chapel Boulevard on a 40.2-acre site 26 miles northwest of Downtown Dallas, the commercial component of Shivers Farm will comprise roughly 128,000 square feet of retail and a 33,000 square feet of office space across nine buildings. bullets: Madison Realty Capital closes $77M construction loan for Trademark/Harrison Street JV Shivers Farm, Southlake
Mixed-use: 37 single-family lots, 161K SF retail/office, 35.5K SF Whole Foods (first Southlake location)
Anchor grocery and master-planned mix on 40-acre site 26 miles NW of Downtown Dallas signals DFW suburban growth
stories.summary: Trademark Property Company and Harrison Street Asset Management have secured $77 million in construction financing from Madison Realty Capital for Shivers Farm, a mixed-use development in Southlake, Texas. The 40.2-acre project includes 37 single-family residential lots, 161,000 square feet of retail and office space anchored by a 35,500-square-foot Whole Foods—the grocer's first Southlake location. The development is only grocery-anchored retail property north of SH 114 within a three-mile radius.
stories.impact: Southlake's anchor grocery deployment (Whole Foods' first location in the city) and large capital commitment signal strong population and household formation growth in this DFW northwest corridor. For multifamily developers, this marks a window to acquire land and develop rental housing within 2–5 miles of Shivers Farm; the new grocery anchor will drive daytime population, job creation, and retail captive base—all supporting renter purchasing power and reducing vacancy risk in new-build apartments nearby.

stories.title: CBRE Investment Management Acquires $1.6B Net-Lease Portfolio
stories.excerpt: CBRE Investment Management is placing a big bet on the net-lease business. CBRE Investment Management — the $155 billion global investment arm of CBRE — announced Wednesday that it acquired Tenet Equity’s $1.6 billion net-lease platform that includes 208 assets in 39 states encompassing 12 million square feet of commercial real estate. The net-lease portfolio — where the tenants typically pay a lower base rent but must cover a building’s operating expenses, such as taxes, insurance and maintenance — is fully leased to middle-market industrial tenants, with an average lease term of roughly 17 years, according to CBRE. CBRE IM will partner with Tenet Equity — a sale-leaseback specialist and capital provider — on managing the assets and growing the partnership’s net-lease platform, appointing senior portfolio manager Akash Shivashankara to lead that effort. Adam Gallistel, co-CEO and chief investment officer of CBRE Investment Management, noted in a statement that the net-lease sector is a hedge against persistent inflation due to its long lease terms and lack of capital expenditures. “We are excited to deliver compelling investment opportunities to our clients by pairing our portfolio management and execution capabilities — together with the net-lease resources of CBRE Group — with Tenet and its proven track record of sourcing and managing mission-critical real estate,” said Gallistel. Truist Securities advised CBRE Investment Management on the transaction. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: CBRE Investment Management acquires Tenet Equity's $1.6B net-lease portfolio: 208 assets, 39 states, 12M SF
Fully leased to middle-market industrial tenants; average lease term ~17 years
Institutional capital aggregating and holding long-term net-lease product; limited direct multifamily relevance
stories.summary: CBRE Investment Management has acquired Tenet Equity's $1.6 billion net-lease platform comprising 208 assets across 39 states totaling 12 million square feet of commercial real estate. The portfolio is fully leased to middle-market industrial tenants with an average lease term of approximately 17 years. CBRE IM will partner with Tenet Equity on portfolio management and platform growth.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. This transaction reflects institutional appetite for long-duration, inflation-hedged industrial net-lease assets—a signal of capital confidence in supply-chain stability and industrial demand, but not a demand or supply driver for apartments. Industrial growth can indirectly support employment and population migration to certain metros, but this portfolio acquisition does not identify specific markets or drive multifamily-specific capital availability.

stories.title: Skip the Script — a Great Seller’s Broker Creates a Strategy Based on Market Feedback
stories.excerpt: One of the biggest mistakes a broker can make when marketing an investment property for sale is prescribing the entire structured marketing process, including bid dates, number of bidding rounds, etc., before the market has had an opportunity to speak. I have seen marketing proposals that lay out a neat sequence: four weeks of marketing, a bid deadline, a second round, a best-and-final round, contract negotiations and a closing. It looks organized. It looks professional. It may even give the seller comfort that there is a carefully constructed plan. After more than four decades of selling investment properties in New York City, I believe that that approach fundamentally misunderstands how a successful competitive process works. A broker representing a seller absolutely needs a strategy, but the strategy should never become a script. Robert Knakal. PHOTO: Patrick McMullan/Patrick McMullan via Getty Images The objective is not to execute a determined number of rounds. The objective is to maximize the seller’s proceeds while optimizing the probability that the transaction actually closes. Those are very different things. The first bid deadline is one of the most important moments in a marketing campaign, and even the timing of that deadline requires judgment. Setting it too early can be just as damaging as setting it too late. A broker may want to create urgency by announcing a quick deadline, but urgency without sufficient market exposure can backfire badly. If the property has not been adequately exposed, buyers have not had enough time to underwrite it, decision-makers have not had time to get comfortable, and the broker has not generated sufficient competitive tension, the deadline may arrive with disappointing participation. Once that happens, the seller can find himself or herself chasing the market rather than having the market chase him or her. stories.title: Broadcom Acquires Irvine Headquarters Campus
stories.excerpt: PRP Real Assets, a privately held real estate investment and management company headquartered in Washington, DC, has sold the Broadcom Corporate Campus in Irvine. Broadcom acquired the property from PRP for $325 million. The 660,893-square-foot campus within the Irvine Spectrum District consists of two five-story office buildings located at 15101 and 15191 Alton Pkwy. Completed in 2017 and 2018, the campus was designed by Gensler as Broadcom’s corporate headquarters with significant research-and-development capabilities and includes 2,989 parking spaces across its 9.6-acre site. “Broadcom’s decision to acquire the campus underscores the property’s importance to the company’s operations and validates the principles behind our Mission-Critical Net Lease strategy,” said Paul C. Dougherty, president of PRP Real Assets. “The campus combines a high-quality asset, a strong tenant and an irreplaceable location in one of the nation’s leading technology markets. We are pleased to have delivered an excellent outcome for our investors and appreciate Broadcom’s collaborative approach throughout the transaction.” The post Broadcom Acquires Irvine Headquarters Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Broadcom acquires own Irvine Corporate Campus from PRP Real Assets for $325M
660K SF, two five-story buildings (2017–2018), 9.6 acres in Irvine Spectrum District
Corporate HQ purchase reflects stability but does not alter broader Irvine tech-employment trajectory
stories.summary: Broadcom has acquired its corporate campus in Irvine from PRP Real Assets for $325 million. The 660,893-square-foot facility consists of two five-story office buildings completed in 2017 and 2018, with 2,989 parking spaces on 9.6 acres within the Irvine Spectrum District. The purchase underscores the property's strategic value to Broadcom's operations.
stories.impact: Broadcom's decision to own rather than lease its HQ signals long-term Irvine commitment and capital confidence, which supports indirect multifamily demand through stable high-wage employment in the Orange County tech corridor. However, office ownership does not directly inform apartment supply, cost, or near-term rental demand; developers should monitor Broadcom's headcount and hiring plans in Irvine for stronger employment-driven rental demand signals.

stories.title: Trammell Crow, Arlington Partnering on $123M Downtown Mixed-Use Project
stories.excerpt: The Arlington City Council has approved an agreement that will transform the largest remaining area of surface parking in central Downtown into a major mixed-use development while also delivering new City-owned assets, public parking and infrastructure. Trammell Crow Company will acquire the privately owned property needed for the development and convey that land to the City. Arlington will retain ownership and ground lease the development site back to the developer for 99 years. The project, located around the City Office Tower near Abram and Mesquite streets, will include at least 390 market-rate residential units, 31,250 square feet of office space, at least 8,000 square feet of restaurant and retail space, and a 600-space structured parking garage. Trammell Crow Company is required to invest at least $123 million in the development. Through the partnership, Arlington will acquire the land underlying the development, a new 31,250-square-foot office for the City’s Water Utilities Department, and significant new public infrastructure. The post Trammell Crow, Arlington Partnering on $123M Downtown Mixed-Use Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Trammell Crow partners with Arlington, TX on $123M downtown mixed-use project; Trammell acquires & conveys land to City
City ground leases site back to developer 99 years; includes 390+ market-rate units, office, retail, parking garage
Mixed-use infill with significant public infrastructure investment; signals Arlington downtown activation and rental demand
stories.summary: Trammell Crow Company and the City of Arlington have approved a public-private partnership to develop a $123 million mixed-use project on the largest remaining surface parking area in downtown Arlington. Trammell Crow will acquire privately held land and convey it to the city, which will ground lease the development site back for 99 years. The project will deliver at least 390 market-rate residential units, 31,250 square feet of office, 8,000 square feet of retail/restaurant, and a 600-space parking garage.
stories.impact: Strong signal of Arlington's downtown activation strategy and multifamily-friendly zoning/entitlement environment. The 390+ market-rate apartment component in a city-partnered development demonstrates demand visibility and public support for residential density in downtown Arlington. For developers, this validates Arlington's rental absorption fundamentals and suggests a widening window for additional rental housing projects in the downtown core; the public infrastructure investment will enhance long-term resident appeal and reduce project-level capital burdens.

stories.title: MassHousing Closes on Financing for Swampscott Affordable Development
stories.excerpt: MassHousing has closed on the final financing for the 114-unit The Westcott in Swampscott, developed by WinnCompanies on a former industrial site following approval by the Town of Swampscott. The $14 million in permanent financing was the final financing piece of the $69.1-million development, which was completed with two transactions involving 4% and 9% Low Income Housing Tax Credits. MassHousing additionally proved $12.2 million in tax credit bridge financing and $2.2 million in workforce housing financing for a project total of $28.4 million. Other financing sources included $37.5 million in federal and state LIHTCs, $38.7 million in construction financing from Bank of America, $7 million in America Rescue Plan Act financing through the Massachusetts Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities (EOHLC), an additional $3 million in ARPA financing through the Affordable Housing Trust Fund, $5.4 million in direct EOHLC financing, $246,000 in local HOME financing and $49,000 in Swampscott Affordable Housing Trust financing. The MBTA provided an easement for the creation of additional resident parking. The mixed-income community opened in July 2025. The post MassHousing Closes on Financing for Swampscott Affordable Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MassHousing closes $14M permanent financing for 114-unit Westcott affordable housing, Swampscott
Total project cost $69.1M; funded via 4%/9% LIHTCs, ARPA, MassHousing, Bank of America, local sources
Signals robust affordable housing capital and entitlement support in Massachusetts coastal markets
stories.summary: MassHousing has closed $14 million in permanent financing for The Westcott, a 114-unit affordable housing development in Swampscott, developed by WinnCompanies on a former industrial site. The $69.1 million total project cost was funded through 4% and 9% Low Income Housing Tax Credits, MassHousing programs, Bank of America construction financing, ARPA funding, and local affordable housing trust contributions.
stories.impact: Strong availability of affordable housing capital (LIHTCs, ARPA, state agency financing, CRA lending) in Massachusetts supports feasibility for mixed-income and affordable development in coastal metros. For market-rate multifamily developers, this signals robust public support for density and adaptive reuse, reducing entitlement risk for residential projects near transit and employment centers in Eastern Massachusetts; developers should consider layered financing structures combining tax credits and senior debt to unlock higher-density, mixed-income projects.

stories.title: Diversified to Break Ground on 100K-SF Scottsdale Lakefront Development
stories.excerpt: Diversified Partners will officially break ground in two weeks on The Lakefront at Scottsdale, its approximately 100,000-square-foot mixed-use redevelopment. The dated mixed-use venture will undergo a major conversion. The landmark Scottsdale waterfront property will include dining, retail, office space and gathering. The site was home to The Charthouse, which opened its doors in 1984 and just closed last year. The property is being redeveloped into a hospitality-driven waterfront destination featuring signature restaurants and outdoor dining, boutique and experiential retail, Class A office space and public gathering areas. Longtime tenant Forever Living Products is staying put in the upgraded office space. At the groundbreaking, at 7501 E. McCormick Parkway, Diversified Partners will officially announce three restaurant and café concepts joining The Lakefront: La La Land Kind Cafe, V Modern Italian, and SUSHISAMBA. WHEN:9:30–11 a.m. Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026 WHERE:The Lakefront at Scottsdale7501 E. McCormick ParkwayScottsdale, AZ 85258 The post Diversified to Break Ground on 100K-SF Scottsdale Lakefront Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Diversified Partners breaks ground on ~100K SF mixed-use Lakefront redevelopment, Scottsdale, AZ
Former Charthouse (closed 2023) converted to dining, retail, office, gathering spaces; three restaurant concepts announced
Waterfront hospitality-driven activation signals Scottsdale demand and experiential retail/F&B anchor for mixed-use
stories.summary: Diversified Partners is breaking ground on The Lakefront at Scottsdale, a 100,000-square-foot mixed-use redevelopment of the former Charthouse property on Scottsdale's waterfront. The project will feature signature restaurants and outdoor dining, boutique retail, Class A office space, and public gathering areas. Three restaurant and café concepts have been announced: La La Land Kind Cafe, V Modern Italian, and SUSHISAMBA.
stories.impact: Waterfront mixed-use redevelopment anchored by experiential dining and retail in Scottsdale signals strong consumer demand and rental population growth in the market. For multifamily developers, this validates Scottsdale's ability to attract and retain high-income residents seeking lifestyle amenities; developers should prioritize sites within 0.5–1.5 miles of The Lakefront for Class A rental projects targeting professionals and empty-nesters drawn to walkable, amenity-rich neighborhoods with premium F&B and retail options.
